An Act to separate the Australian Energy Regulator from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, and for related purposes

content.p: This Act is the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Australian Energy Regulator Separation) Act 2025.

Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.
Note: This table relates only to the provisions of this Act as originally enacted. It will not be amended to deal with any later amendments of this Act.
Any information in column 3 of the table is not part of this Act. Information may be inserted in this column, or information in it may be edited, in any published version of this Act.

Legislation that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

hcontainer.name: item
hcontainer.heading: Subdivision B of Division 4 of Part IIIAA

content.p: Repeal the Subdivision, substitute:
Subdivision B—Staff of the AER etc.
(1) The staff of the AER must be persons engaged under the Public Service Act 1999.
(2) For the purposes of the Public Service Act 1999:
the AER Chair and the APS employees assisting the AER Chair together constitute a Statutory Agency; and
the AER Chair is the Head of that Statutory Agency.
The AER may be assisted by:

(a) officers and employees of Agencies (within the meaning of the Public Service Act 1999), and of authorities of the Commonwealth, whose services are made available to the AER in connection with the performance of any of the AER’s functions; and
persons whose services are made available under arrangements made under subsection (2).
The AER may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, make an arrangement with the appropriate authority or officer of:
a State or Territory government; or
a State or Territory government authority;
under which the government or authority makes officers or employees available to the AER to perform services in connection with the performance of any of the AER’s functions.
An arrangement under subsection (2) may provide for the Commonwealth to reimburse a State or Territory with respect to the services of a person to whom the arrangement relates.
When performing services for the AER under this section, a person is subject to the directions of the AER.
The AER may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, engage persons to give advice to, and perform services for, the AER.
The terms and conditions of engagement are as determined by the AER.

This item applies in relation to a delegation if:

hcontainer.name: clause
hcontainer.heading: Transfer of documents to the AER

content.p: This item applies to a document if:
immediately before the commencement day, the document was in the possession of the Commission; and
the document was:
given to or received by the Commission; or
brought into existence;
in relation to the performance of a function of the AER under Division 3 of Part IIIAA of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010.
The documents may be transferred to the AER on or after the commencement day.
Note: Any documents transferred are Commonwealth records for the purposes of the Archives Act 1983.

(1) Regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of State/Territory energy law in subsection 4(1) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010, and in force immediately before the commencement day, also have effect, during the transitional period, as if those regulations had been made for the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of AER State/Territory energy law in section 44AB of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010, as amended by the amending Act.

(2) For the purposes of subitem (1), the transitional period is the period beginning at the start of the commencement day and ending immediately before regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (c) of the definition of AER State/Territory energy law in section 44AB of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010, as amended by the amending Act, take effect.
The ACCC Enterprise Agreement:
continues, on and from the commencement day, to cover and apply to APS employees:
who it covered and applied to immediately before the commencement day; and
who, on the commencement day, are members of the staff of the AER; and

covers and applies to APS employees who are at the classification levels covered by the ACCC Enterprise Agreement whose employment as a member of the staff of the AER commences on or after the commencement day.
On and after the commencement day, the ACCC Enterprise Agreement covers and applies to the AER Chair as the Agency Head of the APS employees who are members of the staff of the AER.
This item does not prevent the variation or termination of the ACCC Enterprise Agreement in accordance with law.
This item does not prevent the terms and conditions of employment of APS employees who are members of the staff of the AER from being varied on or after the commencement day:
in accordance with those terms and conditions; or
by or under a law.
(5) This item does not affect the operation of section 58 of the Fair Work Act 2009.
Note: Section 58 of that Act deals with the interaction between one or more enterprise agreements.
On and from the commencement day, the ACCC Enterprise Agreement has effect in relation to the AER as if:
a reference to the Chairperson were a reference to the AER Chair; and
a reference to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, or the ACCC, were a reference to the AER.
To avoid doubt, this item does not prevent the ACCC Enterprise Agreement from being varied or terminated on or after the commencement day.
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Schedule to be prescribed by the rules; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Schedule.
Without limiting subitem (1), the rules may prescribe matters of a transitional nature (including prescribing any saving or application provisions) relating to:
the application of the ACCC Enterprise Agreement to members of the staff of the AER who are APS employees; or
the enactment of the amending Act.
To avoid doubt, the rules may not do the following:
create an offence or civil penalty;
provide powers of:
arrest or detention; or
entry, search or seizure;
impose a tax;
set an amount to be appropriated from the Consolidated Revenue Fund;
(e) directly amend the text of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 or the amending Act.
This Schedule (other than subitem (3)) does not limit the rules that may be made for the purposes of subitem (1).
